Before you can fix something, you need to understand what's broken. In this case, what's broken is approximately everything.

They say knowledge is power. In this case, knowledge is mostly just depressing. But you need it, the way you need to know your house is on fire before you can put it out.

## The Daily Body Count

Every day, 150,000 [humans die](problem/cost-of-disease.qmd) from disease and aging. That's fifty 9/11s. Per day. Including weekends and holidays.

![Every day, 50 times as many people die from being old and sick as died on 9/11. You started two wars over 9/11. For aging, you bought face cream and called it a day.](/assets/images/problem/problem-section-daily-numbers-bw-academic.jpg)

When one thing kills 3,000 people, it's a tragedy and you start wars. When diseases kill 50 times that every day, it's called "natural causes," which is Latin for "you couldn't be bothered."

After the first 9/11, America invaded two countries and spent $2 trillion. After the fifty daily 9/11s, humanity shrugs and wonders what's for lunch.

## Where the Money Goes

**Killing each other:** {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} per year
**Curing diseases:** {{< var global_med_research_spending >}} per year

The real bottleneck isn't research funding. It's testing which treatments actually work. Governments worldwide spend {{< var global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}} annually on clinical trials, a {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} ratio, which in technical terms is called "[having your priorities backwards](problem/cost-of-war.qmd)."

![Humanity spends 2.72 trillion on weapons and 4.5 billion on testing medicine. That's 604 times more money for killing than curing. You named yourselves Homo sapiens, which is Latin for 'wise man.' The irony is exquisite.](/assets/images/problem/problem-section-where-the-money-goes-bw-academic.jpg)

## On Medical Research

Since 1970, the [National Institutes of Health](problem/nih-fails-2-institute-health.qmd) has spent over $1 trillion studying diseases.

Diseases cured: Zero.

Of its {{< var nih_annual_budget >}} annual budget, only {{< var nih_clinical_trials_spending_pct >}} goes to actual drug trials in humans. The other 97% goes to studying mice, building buildings, and publishing papers nobody reads. The system operates at 2% of its potential capacity to save lives.

![America spent $55,500 per patient to test COVID treatments. Britain spent $500. Same disease, same planet, same year. Different levels of commitment to wasting money.](/assets/images/problem/problem-section-on-medical-research-bw-academic.jpg)

## On the FDA

The [FDA](problem/fda-is-unsafe-and-ineffective.qmd) makes drugs {{< var recovery_trial_cost_reduction_factor >}} times more expensive than necessary. It takes {{< var drug_discovery_to_approval_years >}} and {{< var pharma_drug_development_cost_current >}} to get a drug from discovery to patient. That's longer than it took to build the pyramids. The pharaohs didn't have to file quarterly progress reports in triplicate. Ninety-five percent of diseases have zero approved treatments because the FDA is excellent at preventing any drugs from reaching people.

![Oxford tests drugs for $500 per patient. The FDA does it for $41,000. Both use the same scientific method, discovered in the 17th century. Innovation takes time.](/assets/images/problem/problem-section-on-the-fda-bw-academic.jpg)

## On What War Costs

Humanity spends {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} every year on war. That works out to {{< var global_military_spending_per_capita_annual >}} per human on Earth for death tools.

![One submarine costs the same as 1,000 cancer research labs. The submarine sinks things. The labs might cure leukemia. You bought the submarine.](/assets/images/problem/problem-section-on-what-war-costs-bw-academic.jpg)

This budget includes:

- Nuclear bombs ({{< var global_warhead_count_nounit >}} of them, because one fewer wouldn't destroy Earth thoroughly enough)
- Bullets (many)
- AI murder robots (the future is here and it's disappointing)
- Fighter jets that cost more than hospitals
- Submarines (one submarine = 1,000 cancer research labs)
- Probably some kind of earthquake machine

Your personal lifetime contribution to the murder budget is $74,259. You could have bought a really nice casket instead. Or, and this is just a thought, not needed a casket quite so soon.

The interesting thing about having {{< var global_warhead_count_nounit >}} nuclear warheads is that after the first {{< var nuclear_winter_warhead_threshold_nounit >}}, you're just showing off. You can only destroy Earth once. The rest are for what, exactly? Destroying Earth's ghost?

## On What Disease Costs

Disease extracts {{< var global_disease_economic_burden_annual >}} from humanity annually in welfare losses ({{< var global_annual_daly_burden_nounit >}} avoidable DALYs at {{< var standard_economic_qaly_value_usd >}}/QALY). That includes 10 million cancer deaths per year and 2 billion people living with chronic diseases.

{{< include figures/trial-access-disparity-chart.qmd >}}

If disease were a country, it would be the richest country on Earth by a factor of ten. Unfortunately, disease doesn't have a flag or an army, so nobody invades it.

Out of {{< var current_disease_patients_global >}} suffering from chronic disease, only {{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} get to participate in clinical trials annually. That's {{< var current_patient_participation_rate >}}. Half would volunteer if asked. You're turning away 99.6% of willing participants.

## On Democracy

A Princeton study found [0% correlation](problem/unrepresentative-democracy.qmd) between what the public wants and what policies get enacted. Zero. Not "low." Not "disappointing." Zero. Your democracy has the same correlation with your preferences as a coin flip has with your breakfast order.

![Military contractors spend $250 million on lobbying and get $850 billion in contracts. That's a 340,000 percent return. You voted and got a sticker. Both are forms of civic participation.](/assets/images/problem/problem-section-on-democracy-bw-academic.jpg)

When the humans you pay to make the killing things want $100 billion, they spend $55 million lobbying for it. That's a 1,813% return on investment. When you want healthcare, you have approximately zero dollars to lobby with. You spent it all on healthcare. Or you're dead, which significantly reduces your lobbying capacity.

Meanwhile, the people who regulate industries used to work for those industries. They'll work for them again after they're done "regulating." It's called the [revolving door](problem/unrepresentative-democracy.qmd), and it spins in one direction: toward money.

## On the Fixed Pie

Money isn't real, but resources are. Earth has 8 billion human brains. Every MIT graduate building missiles is not [curing cancer](economics/central-banks.qmd). Every brilliant physicist designing warheads is not designing MRI machines. You have a fixed number of geniuses. You are using them to build things that kill other geniuses. Switzerland spends {{< var switzerland_defense_spending_pct >}} of GDP on military and has {{< var switzerland_gdp_per_capita_k >}} GDP per capita. America spends {{< var us_military_spending_pct_gdp >}} and has $76,000.

![Switzerland pays doctors more than generals and has a higher GDP per capita than America. America pays generals more than doctors and has more aircraft carriers. Different priorities, different outcomes.](/assets/images/problem/problem-section-on-the-fixed-pie-bw-academic.jpg)

The solution isn't to print more money for medical research. The solution is to change the ratio. Take money from the killing budget, give it to the not-dying budget. This is called "arithmetic," which is apparently a controversial field of mathematics.
